title: Sony launches the PlayStation 2 video game console in Japan
content: Sony released the PlayStation 2 in Japan, marking the debut of the sixth generation of video game consoles. With its integrated DVD player and powerful Emotion Engine processor, it quickly went on to become the best-selling home video game console of all time.

title: NASDAQ Composite hits historic peak of 5,048 before tech crash
content: The NASDAQ Composite Index reached an all-time high of 5,048.62, capping a 400 percent rise over five years driven by intense speculation in internet and technology stocks. Stretched valuations reached extreme levels, with major technology darlings trading at price-to-earnings multiples exceeding 140x to 160x, setting the stage for an unprecedented market correction.

title: Burning Up: Warning: Internet companies are running out of cash -- fast
content: Barron's published a landmark cover story analyzing 207 publicly traded dot-com companies, revealing that 51 firms—over a quarter of the sample—would completely exhaust their cash reserves within 12 months. The report exposed unsustainable burn rates across the internet sector, shattering market confidence in growth-over-profit business models.

title: MicroStrategy plummets after financial restatement wipes out billions
content: Business intelligence software developer MicroStrategy announced a major restatement of its financial results for the prior two years due to improper revenue recognition accounting. Shares suffered a catastrophic 62 percent single-day drop, wiping out $6 billion in founder market wealth and signaling severe corporate governance vulnerabilities across tech startups.

title: LimeWire peer-to-peer file sharing software is released
content: Software developer Mark Gorton released LimeWire, a free peer-to-peer file sharing client running on the Gnutella network. It rapidly grew into one of the most widely used applications for sharing digital music and files across the consumer web.

title: From Boo.com to Boo.gone: European fashion dot-com collapses into liquidation
content: High-profile European online fashion retailer Boo.com collapsed into receivership after burning through $188 million in capital in just six months. The company fell victim to lavish marketing spending, complex non-functional website design, and an inability to secure additional venture funding when market sentiment shifted.

title: Human Genome Project and Celera Genomics announce initial draft sequence
content: In a joint announcement with US President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair, leaders of the Human Genome Project and Celera Genomics revealed the completion of the first working draft of the human genome sequence, ushering in a new era for computational biology.

title: Nokia unveils the iconic 3310 mobile phone handset
content: Nokia announced the Nokia 3310, a compact mobile phone featuring customizable Xpress-on covers, SMS chat capabilities, and pre-installed mobile games including Snake II. It became a global commercial juggernaut, selling over 126 million units worldwide.

title: Microsoft releases Windows Millennium Edition (Windows Me)
content: Microsoft officially launched Windows Millennium Edition, targeted at home PC users. It served as the final consumer operating system built on the monolithic Windows 9x codebase before Microsoft unified its OS family under the Windows NT kernel with Windows XP.

title: Google launches AdWords self-service advertising program
content: Google launched AdWords with 350 initial advertisers, introducing a self-service portal for placing targeted keyword ads on search result pages. This launch established the core monetization model for modern search engine business.

title: Expedition 1 arrives at the International Space Station
content: Astronaut William Shepherd and cosmonauts Sergei Krikalev and Yuri Gidzenko docked with the International Space Station, becoming its first resident crew (Expedition 1) and establishing uninterrupted human presence in low Earth orbit.

title: Pets.com, Sock Puppet's Home, Will Close
content: In the latest example of the difficulties facing Internet retailers, Pets.com announced yesterday that it was closing down its operations. The company was losing money and found itself unable to raise more cash or to find a buyer.

title: Intel debuts the Pentium 4 processor based on NetBurst architecture
content: Intel released its long-awaited Pentium 4 desktop processor line, introducing the NetBurst microarchitecture designed for high clock speeds and hyper-pipelined performance to compete in the high-end PC marketplace.

title: Iron laws of the market bring a sharp dose of reality to the virtual business world
content: First it was tulips, then it was shares in the South Sea Company. Now the dot.coms have been added to that dubious hall of fame - the roll call of speculative bubbles that have punctuated the history of financial markets.

title: eToys files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy following holiday sales shortfall
content: Pioneering online toy merchant eToys.com filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after reporting $247 million in debt and fourth-quarter holiday sales that reached less than half of previous projections, leading to complete asset liquidation.
source: CNN Money / The Wall Street Journal

title: Yahoo! CEO Tim Koogle steps down amid severe revenue warning
content: Yahoo! Chief Executive Officer Tim Koogle announced his resignation alongside a drastic reduction in first-quarter revenue projections. As dot-com startup advertising spending collapsed, Yahoo!'s market valuation plummeted nearly 90 percent from its peak.

title: Cisco Systems announces massive $2.25 billion inventory write-down and 8,500 layoffs
content: Cisco Systems, briefly the world's most valuable corporation, announced an unprecedented $2.25 billion write-off of unusable raw materials and component inventory. The company announced 8,500 job cuts as telecommunications carriers and enterprise clients abruptly halted hardware capital expenditures.

title: High-speed internet pioneer Excite@Home files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
content: Broadband service provider Excite@Home filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection following mounting debt obligations and failing revenue streams. The downfall highlighted the severe financial stress across merged media and network access providers.

title: Enron files largest bankruptcy in U.S. history following accounting fraud discovery
content: Energy and broadband trading empire Enron Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after losing $63 billion in market value within 47 days. Investigations uncovered complex off-balance-sheet special purpose entities and fraudulent mark-to-market accounting used to conceal billions in debt.

title: Global Crossing files for bankruptcy in massive telecom crash
content: Subsea fiber-optic network builder Global Crossing filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy with $12.4 billion in debt. The collapse was driven by massive global fiber network capacity oversupply and accounting irregularities involving non-cash capacity swaps between telecom carriers.

title: WorldCom files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid $11 billion accounting scandal
content: Telecommunications giant WorldCom filed the largest bankruptcy in American history, carrying $35 billion in debt and $107 billion in assets. An internal audit revealed that executives improperly capitalized over $3.8 billion in normal operating line costs to inflate earnings.
source: VOA News / The New York Times

title: NASDAQ Composite touches cycle trough of 1,139.90, closing 78 percent drawdown
content: The NASDAQ Composite Index fell to its multi-year trough of 1,139.90 points, completing a 78 percent decline from its peak in March 2000. Approximately $5 trillion in market equity value evaporated across the tech sector, leaving fewer than 50 of hundreds of IPO startups as independent survivors.

title: AOL Time Warner posts historic $99 billion annual loss and executive departure
content: AOL Time Warner announced an unprecedented annual net loss of nearly $99 billion for 2002, driven by massive non-cash goodwill write-downs of its America Online division. Chairman Steve Case announced his resignation, cementing the mega-merger as the ultimate symbol of the dot-com bubble's destruction.
